transcript:
Header: 2026-03-04 14:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Nair - Redwood; Marcus Hale (CTO), Sana Ortiz (ML Engineer), Liam Park (Infra) - Starlight Fintech

Summary: quick discovery on latency/throughput requirements, clarifying p95 targets and integration options (Hosted/Dedicated/Private).

00:00 Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll do a quick intro and then jump into your latency and throughput needs.
00:14 Marcus Hale: yeah thanks Jordan, appreciate it. so i run infra at Starlight, we're building realtime transaction monitoring and risk scoring, we need low-latency streaming responses to feed our risk engine.
00:28 Jordan Lee: awesome, can you give us the p95 targets and concurrency you're aiming for?
00:33 Sana Ortiz: for our short-turn prompts—these are ~20-40 tokens after system prompt—we want p95 under 120ms ideally, and sustain about 200 concurrent streaming sessions. for longer summaries (200-400 tokens) p95 can relax to 800-1000ms.
00:53 Priya Nair: ok great. are those streaming token-by-token responses or single-response generation?
00:58 Sana Ortiz: streaming, we need token-level updates to downstream services.
01:03 Liam Park: and we need predictable tail latency during spikes, we can't have p95 double during promos or end-of-day batch windows.
01:12 Jordan Lee: understood. quick qual: what's your current stack and models? are you using managed endpoints or self-hosted?
01:19 Marcus Hale: right now we have a small self-hosted setup running 4x A100s, using a mix of open models and a couple of larger transformer variants. throughput is ok but the ops burden is high, we're exploring Hosted for ease or Dedicated for predictable cost. private on-prem is an option for PCI concerns.
01:36 Priya Nair: got it. for p95 120ms at 200 concurrent streaming sessions, that's a pretty tight requirement depending on model size & sequence length. Have you profiled token/sec per GPU with your models?
01:47 Sana Ortiz: we did some internal tests, roughly 120-180 tokens/sec on our A100 cluster for the smaller model, but tail latencies spike under concurrency.
02:00 Jordan Lee: ok, helpful. typical tradeoffs: Hosted gives fastest time-to-value but multi-tenant variance; Dedicated gives isolation/predictable latency and capacity; Private gives full control but more ops. for p95 under 120ms for short prompts, Dedicated or Private is usually where customers land.
02:20 Marcus Hale: what's Redwood's approach to batching and KV cache? we need consistent streaming.
02:27 Priya Nair: we do continuous batching with dynamic batch sizes and prefix/KV caching. streaming is implemented so tokens can be flushed to the client as generated; we have per-route latency SLOs that can prioritize low-latency traffic and limit batching for those routes. caching helps if many requests share context or system prompts.
02:45 Sana Ortiz: can you guarantee no extra reordering or large chunked flushes that break our token-by-token expectations?
02:51 Priya Nair: we aim to preserve streaming order; in Dedicated deployments you can tune batching windows to minimize aggressive batching. there are quantization and kernel selection knobs to trade accuracy for perf.
03:05 Liam Park: about benchmarking — we'd like to run token/sec benchmarks and p95 latency tests. what's the standard approach?
03:11 Jordan Lee: we typically do a 48-hour benchmark run using your representative prompt sets and concurrency profile. we instrument p50/p95/p99, token/sec, throughput, and cost per token. if you want, we can run on Hosted first as a quick baseline, then Dedicated pilot to compare.
03:27 Marcus Hale: ok, and will Redwood simulate our concurrency pattern (sporadic spikes)?
03:31 Priya Nair: yes, we run traffic patterns including ramp-ups and bursts. we also show caching/batching benefits and KV-cache hit rates.
03:40 Sana Ortiz: what about streaming throughput numbers — tokens/sec per GPU for say a 13B open model vs 70B?
03:46 Priya Nair: approximate numbers — on our optimized runtime, a 13B FP16/INT8 variant typically 600-1200 tokens/sec per A100-ish equivalent depending on seq length and decoding settings. 70B is much lower, often 80-250 tokens/sec. those are broad ranges, exact depends on quantization, KV cache behavior, and model-specific kernels.
04:06 Marcus Hale: interesting — our internal numbers were lower for 13B, so we'd like Redwood to run the same prompts.
04:11 Jordan Lee: absolutely. also important: routing and fallback policies. if Dedicated is saturated, we can route to a cheaper variant with slightly higher latency but keep service available. is that acceptable?
04:22 Marcus Hale: yes as long as degradation is graceful and audited. compliance is huge for us — PCI and SOC2 and SSO with our Okta.
04:31 Priya Nair: we have SOC2, SSO (SAML), RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integrations for Private deployments. we'll share the security pack.
04:41 Sana Ortiz: can you share specifics on encryption at rest and in transit for Dedicated?
04:45 Jordan Lee: Dedicated supports customer-managed keys via KMS for model artifacts and can integrate VPC peering. we can include network diagrams in the security pack.
04:54 Liam Park: ok, timeline wise — we want a pilot in 2-3 weeks, decision within a month if performance meets p95 targets.
05:02 Jordan Lee: that seems doable. we'll propose a pilot plan: 48-hour bench + a 2-week dedicated pilot if bench passes.
05:09 Sana Ortiz: for the bench, we will provide 3 prompt sets: short-turn fraud signals, medium summaries, and long investigative chains.
05:18 Priya Nair: great — can you also provide concurrency distribution (80% short-turn streaming, 15% medium, 5% long)?
05:26 Marcus Hale: yes, we'll drop that into the shared folder.
05:29 Jordan Lee: quick clarifying q — are you planning to use streaming WebSocket connections or HTTP SSE?
05:34 Liam Park: websocket for lower latency, yes.
05:37 Priya Nair: we support both; WebSocket gives lower end-to-end latency, and we can instrument token-level latency.
05:44 Sana Ortiz: what about quantization and model variants? we're willing to use int8 if accuracy holds.
05:49 Priya Nair: we recommend profile-driven quantization: we'll run evals on your prompt sets to quantify quality delta (exact-match / rouge / custom metrics) vs perf gains. often int8 yields 2-4x perf boost for larger models.
06:02 Jordan Lee: any blockers on data residency or on-prem?
06:06 Marcus Hale: for PCI we prefer Dedicated within our cloud account or Private on-prem. need to evaluate cost.
06:12 Jordan Lee: we can size a Dedicated pool with VPC peering so you control ingress/egress. cost estimates we'll include in the pricing doc.
06:19 Sana Ortiz: queue: about tail latency — you mentioned per-route SLOs, how do you enforce them?
06:24 Priya Nair: we have dynamic priority queues: low-latency routes get prioritized execution and lower batch windows. if the system detects SLO violation risk, it can fall back to a faster model variant or throttle non-critical traffic. metrics and traces are visible in the Console.
06:40 Marcus Hale: nice. for our risk engine, even occasional spikes above p95 are problematic. what's typical p99 on Dedicated?
06:46 Priya Nair: p99 depends but Dedicated is much tighter — p99 might be around 1.5-2x p95 for short prompts; the exact number depends on spike patterns and model.
06:58 Liam Park: do you provide token-level cost breakdowns? we need to estimate monthly spend at target throughput.
07:02 Jordan Lee: yep Console shows per-token cost, per-route cost, and per-model breakdown. we'll calculate based on bench results.
07:10 Sana Ortiz: any limitations on websocket connection count? we're looking at 200 concurrent streaming sessions initially.
07:15 Priya Nair: Dedicated can be sized for that easily; we'll propose a pool with headroom. for Hosted, multi-tenant spike protection exists but Dedicated is recommended for strict p95 targets.
07:25 Marcus Hale: great. are there known model incompatibilities or kernels missing for some open weights?
07:29 Priya Nair: sometimes uncommon architectures need additional kernel work; we keep a model catalog of supported/verified models. if your model isn't verified, we'll onboard and run a perf profile as part of the pilot.
07:40 Jordan Lee: recap and next steps: we'll send pricing and Dedicated sizing, Priya will schedule benchmark and run 48-hour test, Marcus will upload prompts and concurrency profile, and we'll share security docs. decision timeline: 3-4 weeks.
07:55 Marcus Hale: perfect. thanks, talk soon.

Transcript notes: transcription contains occasional speaker mislabels, filler words, and minor transcription artifacts.

End of call.
